subject: E2E latency gate: hosted vs incumbent — post-demo playbook
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jenny Park <jenny.park@crescenttx.com>, Samuel Osei <s.osei@crescenttx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: E2E latency gate: hosted vs incumbent — post-demo playbook

Hi Jenny / Samuel —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Short recap and a proposed playbook to qualify the p95 / p99 E2E latency gate for Crescent’s assistant workflows when comparing hosted Redwood vs your incumbent provider. I want this to be concrete so we can converge quickly.

High-level targets (customer stated):
- p95 end-to-end (inference + network + client parse) target: <= 220 ms under steady-state traffic
- p99 end-to-end target: <= 480 ms with allowance for short tails during burst windows

Key constraints you emphasized:
- Typical concurrency target: 200–300 concurrent inference sessions (web clients)
- Burst tolerance: short spikes up to ~900 concurrent requests for up to 2 minutes
- Streaming: chunked/partial response streaming used for long outputs (clients expect first-token within 120–150 ms)
- Safety margin: 99th percentile across your east-coast user population is most important first pass

Proposed next steps (playbook):
1) Crescent: share a 48-hour representative traffic profile (arrival rate by minute, payload sizes, streaming vs non-streaming mix). Prefer CSV; I referenced a template as an attachment for easy fill.
2) Redwood: run A/B pairwise runs — (A) hosted Redwood pipeline (pin to model x.y.z) vs (B) incumbent provider — with identical traffic replay and tracing enabled.
3) Joint acceptance criteria: p95 and p99 measured end-to-end at the client boundary (we’ll provide a small agent you can run in your staging region to capture timing).
4) Runbook & gating: Ben will provide the technical runbook for traffic shaping, KV cache warmup, and streaming concurrency limits. We’ll include fallback policies if p99 exceeds gates.
5) POC kickoff: agree on a 4-hour sanity run + 24-hour sustained run window.

Attachments: I attached a very small traffic template to make step (1) quick: crescent_poc_traffic_profile.csv (stub).

Open questions for Crescent (please respond inline):
- Can you provide historical 95/99 client-side tail latencies for the last 30 days under production?
- Are there any IP blocks / egress constraints we need to be aware of for the agent that collects traces?
- Which region should we run in first (us-east-1 preferred unless you ask for eu)?

I’ll loop Ben in with a technical runbook and initial hypothesized knobs that tend to matter (batching window, prefetch/KV warmup, streaming chunk size). If these targets are critical for leadership sign-off, we’ll prioritize the 24-hour sustained run after a short canary.

Thanks — talk soon,

Marissa Cole

Marissa — thanks for the clear write-up. Appreciate the concrete steps. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) We can share a 48-hour traffic dump and a 30-day summary of client-side latencies. I attached the 48-hour CSV as requested — crescent_poc_traffic_profile.csv (stub).
2) For the agent that collects client-side timings: we can run it in our staging cluster (us-east-1) but procurement will need the egress IPs and a short security questionnaire before we allow outbound telemetry.
3) Regarding bursts: our product team wants the hosted run to show graceful degradation in the p99 (i.e., tail increases < 2x baseline during 2-minute bursts). Is Redwood able to simulate your autoscaling/fallback during the 24-hour run, or do we need to trigger manual scaling events?

Can we schedule the 4-hour canary on Tue 2027-03-30 14:00 ET? If that works we’ll freeze traffic and provide a staging endpoint for the agent.

Thank you — attaching the traffic profile now.

Subject: Re: E2E latency gate: hosted vs incumbent — post-demo playbook

Thanks Marissa / Jenny — I sketched a technical runbook & proof artifacts for the comparison runs. Summary of what we’ll measure and how: 

Measurement approach:
- End-to-end timing: client send -> client received final token (we’ll supply a small tracer script to measure accurate wall-clock times).
- Streaming sanity: measure first-token latency and steady-state token pace (tokens/sec) for streaming flows.
- Concurrency profile: we’ll replay your CSV with the same arrival distribution, including the 2-minute spike windows.

Key knobs we will exercise (and why they matter):
- Batching window (ms): affects p95 in steady-state; we’ll sweep 0–25 ms to find breakpoints.
- KV cache warmup: cold-starts can inflate p99; we’ll include a warmup phase before recording metrics.
- Streaming chunk size / client buffer: larger chunks improve throughput but can delay first-token; we’ll test recommended chunk sizes: 32/64/128 tokens.
- Prefetch degree: number of concurrent in-flight requests per GPU; tuned for throughput vs tail.

Preliminary expected bands (for planning only):
- Hosted Redwood (typical): p95 ~ 150–250 ms, p99 ~ 350–600 ms depending on burst shape and warm/cold state.
- Incumbent (as reported): we expect similar p95 but longer p99 tails during the 2-minute spikes; the 2x tail increase Jenny mentioned is plausible.

Run logistics / artifacts I’ll push to the shared Drive and link in HubSpot: 
- Gate report (PDF) with sprints/graphs: redwood_latency-proof-report-20270328.pdf
- Technical runbook & command list: runbook-hosted-vs-incumbent.md
- Dashboards: we’ll provide a temporary Grafana read-only link after the run.

Notes on autoscaling: Redwood’s hosted pool can be configured to allow rapid scale up for the 2-minute spike patterns; we recommend a manual `scale-for-burst` step during the canary so we can observe both modes (no-scale vs scale-on-demand). If you want us to demonstrate automatic fallback, we’ll enable it during the 24-hour run.

Requested from Crescent prior to canary:
- Approve outbound collector IPs (I listed them in the runbook)
- Provide a staging endpoint where the agent can POST traces (or allow our agent to run inside your staging VPC)

I’ll upload the run artifacts now and post links to the folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C4-redwood-crescent
